DIRECTOR OF FOOTBALL — the agreed direction.

Terminal's density and typography, Floodlight's pill button and icon nav, a club-coloured header, and the tappable overview grid from Football Chairman Pro.

Row below: the three directions this came out of, kept for reference.

HOME

Terminal skeleton: mono for every number, a status strip that never leaves screen (cash / wage ratio / FFP), fixed columns.

FC Pro's contribution is the tile grid — eight tap targets, each a live value with a bar under it, so the whole department state reads in one glance without a word of prose. The bar is what the cartoon tiles were really doing: showing state, not just reporting it.

Floodlight's contribution is the lime pill and the icon nav. One saturated colour, one primary action per screen.

SQUAD — the density test

Same header treatment, back chevron and filter in the club band. Status strip carries the constraints you'd otherwise have to go hunting for: registered 24/25, non-homegrown 16/17, wage ratio.

13 rows visible without scrolling versus 8 in the card layouts, and nothing is boxed. Rating is the only coloured column; tags (KNK, BID, HG) are the only other ink.

CLUB COLOUR — readable, always

Painting a header the raw club colour breaks on yellow, white and near-black. The rule: take the primary in HSL, clamp lightness into 10–17%, cap chroma, and keep an untouched 3px strip beneath so the real colour is still on screen.

White primaries fall through to the secondary. Near-blacks lift instead of clamping. Six worst cases shown; every one clears 4.5:1 with white text.

Nothing below the strip is club-coloured.
EARLIER DIRECTIONS — kept for reference, not proposed.
